title: Measure and Compare
objectives: I can compare two things and tell how they are alike and different.
I can measure length and weigh something.
I can tell when two things are equal.
I can find and tell about a pattern.
rationale: Math and science both ask first graders to compare and measure, so the year ends with the words for doing both precisely. Compare is the thinking, measure, length, and weigh are the doing, and equal and pattern are two big ideas children meet in every math lesson. The unit revisits tiny, enormous, narrow, and describe, because comparing sizes uses exactly those describing words, and now children back them up with a measurement.

words.def: Look at how things are alike and different.
words.ex: Let's compare the red apple and the green apple.
words.ex2: We compare two plants to see which one grew taller.
words.nonExample: Counting one pile of blocks does not compare anything.

apps.writing: Use compare to tell how two things are alike or different.

cloze.s: To ___ the two pencils, put them side by side and see which is longer.

cloze2.s: Let's ___ our drawings and see how they are alike.

misuse.s: I compare two toys by only looking at one of them.
misuse.why: To compare you need at least two things. Looking at one toy does not compare.

visual.alt: A red apple and a green apple side by side.

words.def: Find out how big, long, or heavy something is.
words.ex: We measure the desk with a ruler.
words.ex2: Dad will measure the flour for the cake.
words.nonExample: Guessing is not the same as measuring.

apps.academic: Measure the line with a ruler.
apps.writing: Use measure to tell how you find a size.

cloze.s: Use a ruler to ___ how long the pencil is.

cloze2.s: The cook will ___ two cups of rice with a cup.

misuse.s: I measured my pencil by singing a song about it.
misuse.why: To measure is to find a size with a tool. Singing a song does not tell how long it is.

visual.alt: A ruler lying next to a pencil.

words.def: How long something is from end to end.
words.ex: The length of the table is four feet.
words.ex2: We measured the length of the classroom with big steps.
words.nonExample: The color of a rope is not its length.

apps.academic: Measure the length of the string.
apps.writing: Write the length with a number and a unit.

cloze.s: A snake's ___ is how long it is from its head to its tail.

cloze2.s: The ___ of the rope was ten steps from end to end.

misuse.s: The length of the box is the color of the box.
misuse.why: Length tells how long something is. A color does not tell how long.

visual.alt: A ruler beside a long snake.

words.def: Find out how heavy something is.
words.ex: Mom will weigh the apples at the store.
words.ex2: We weigh the puppy on a scale at the vet.
words.nonExample: A ruler does not weigh things; it measures length.

apps.academic: Weigh the object on the scale.
apps.writing: Use weigh to tell how you find how heavy something is.

cloze.s: We use a scale to ___ the fruit and see how heavy it is.

cloze2.s: The vet will ___ the kitten to see how much it grew.

misuse.s: I weigh my backpack by counting how many colors it has.
misuse.why: To weigh is to find how heavy something is. Counting colors does not do that.

visual.alt: A balance scale holding an apple.

words.def: The same in size, number, or amount.
words.ex: The two cups hold equal amounts of juice.
words.ex2: Cut the cake into equal pieces so everyone gets the same.

apps.writing: Use equal to tell how two amounts match.

cloze.s: Each child got an ___ number of stickers, so it was fair.

cloze2.s: Cut the sandwich into two ___ halves so each friend gets the same.

misuse.s: The big pile and the tiny pile were equal in size.
misuse.why: Equal means the same. A big pile and a tiny pile are not the same size.

visual.alt: A balance scale level with a cookie on each side.

words.def: Shapes, colors, or numbers that repeat again and again.
words.ex: The red, blue, red, blue stripes make a pattern.
words.ex2: The rug has a pattern of stars and moons.
words.nonExample: Dots tossed at random do not make a pattern.

senses.def: A guide used to make something, like a shirt.
senses.example: Mom used a pattern to sew the shirt.

apps.academic: Tell what comes next in the pattern.
apps.writing: Use pattern to tell what repeats.

cloze.s: Red, blue, red, blue, red, blue is a color ___.

cloze2.s: The tiles on the floor form a ___ of squares and circles.

misuse.s: The shapes were all mixed up with no order, so it was a pattern.
misuse.why: A pattern repeats in order. Shapes with no order are not a pattern.

visual.alt: Red, blue, and red circles in a row.

passage.title: Measuring the Garden
paras: Lena and Sam measure their garden with a ruler. They compare the length of two rows and find that both are equal. Then they weigh a big pumpkin on a scale. Lena writes the numbers in her notebook. The seeds in the last row make a pattern: one bean, one pea, one bean, one pea.

qs.q: What do Lena and Sam use to measure the garden?
qs.why: The first sentence says they measure the garden with a ruler.

qs.q: What do they find about the two rows?
choices: The rows are equal in length.
qs.why: The story says they compare the length of two rows and both are equal.

qs.q: What is the pattern in the seeds?
qs.why: The story says one bean, one pea, one bean, one pea.

write.prompt: Draw two things. Compare them. Tell which one is longer or heavier.

study.task: Clap the beats in each word: com-pare, meas-ure, length, weigh, e-qual, pat-tern. Which words have only one beat?

sentences: Say how you can measure the length of your desk.
Write a sentence that compares two animals.

given: The two sticks are the same.

I weighed both blocks to compare the heavy red one and the light blue one.

discuss: What can you measure with a ruler? What can you weigh?
Why is it important to cut something into equal parts?

look: gives a number and a unit or a clear step

teacher.overview: Children learn six words for measuring and comparing, then use them to measure a garden and compare two things. The unit revisits tiny, enormous, narrow, and describe.

notes.va.compare.v: Compare needs two things. Put two objects side by side and ask 'How are they alike? How are they different?'. Link to tiny and enormous.
notes.va.measure.v: Measure uses a tool: ruler, cup, or scale. Let children measure with blocks or paper clips first, then a ruler. Guessing comes before measuring, not instead of it.
notes.va.length.n: Length is how long from end to end. Use a string. Children often confuse length with height; both are lengths, but start with a line they can lay down.
notes.va.weigh.v: Weigh uses a scale. A balance scale shows heavier and lighter without numbers. Keep weigh as the doing and weight as the noun for later.
notes.va.equal.adj: Equal means the same. Use two groups with the same number of blocks. Un- plus equal makes unequal, a link to unit 8.
notes.va.pattern.n: A pattern repeats in order. Use colored blocks and ask 'What comes next?'. The sewing sense of pattern is in the senses list and is not taught here.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'I want to compare these two pencils. I measure the length of each one with a ruler. The first is six inches and the second is six inches. They are equal. I weigh them on a scale, too. Now I see a pattern on the first pencil: red, blue, red, blue.'
discuss: What do you measure at home?
Where do you see a pattern in this room?
misconceptions: Measure means to guess how big.
Weigh means to check how tall something is.
extend: Children measure three classroom objects with paper clips and compare the results.
Children make a pattern with blocks and a partner says what comes next.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit measure, compare, and equal the next day with a new set of objects, again at one week, and use them in every math lesson. The words return in grade 2 with similar and contrast.

wida.oral: Partner A measures or weighs two objects and tells the numbers. Partner B says whether they are equal and which is longer or heavier.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (comparar, medir, longitud, pesar, igual, patrón) are not reviewed by a native speaker; longitud is often largo in everyday speech.
Pattern carries a second sense (a guide for sewing) in senses; the unit teaches the repeating-pattern sense.
The unit mentions inches and feet; the examples use the length unit only in simple ways.
